name: Semachiah
overview: Semachiah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted in Scripture as the son of Shemaiah. He is distinguished as the son of a valiant man, indicating a legacy of strength or courage within his family line. Beyond this, the biblical record provides limited additional details about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Semachiah means 'Yahweh sustains, consecrates,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that aligns with the Levite heritage of dedication to God's service. This proper name underscores a connection to divine support and sanctification, although it was not explicitly given by God according to the record.
familyAndRelationships: Semachiah is explicitly identified as the son of Shemaiah, who is described as a valiant man. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for Semachiah beyond this father-son connection.
scriptureSignificance: Semachiah's significance lies primarily in his lineage as the son of Shemaiah, a man noted for valor, which suggests a family of notable standing within the tribe of Levi. His mention in 1 Chronicles 26:7 connects him to the Levitical heritage, emphasizing the importance of faithful and courageous service in God's appointed tribe. Though details are sparse, his identity contributes to the broader biblical testimony of the Levites' role in Israel's worship and community life.
